gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-pau-cin-hau: Noto Sans Pau Cin Hau keeps its curves open-ended, with capitals just a short step above lowercase. And Megrim, angular and futuristic, draws every stroke at a measured thickness with no thick-thin swing.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-phoenician: Angular and futuristic, Megrim holds every stroke to one measured thickness, uppercase included. Noto Sans Phoenician opens its s curves wide at both ends, so paragraphs stay generous and easy going.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-rejang: Futuristic Megrim holds an unvarying line thickness from the first letter to the last. Noto Sans Rejang then gives long text wide, porthole-like counters that keep paragraphs open and easy to follow.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-runic: Sharp, neon-tube Megrim keeps one track width throughout, with a skyward x-height line. Noto Sans Runic brings a big x-height and curves that never close, so long text feels open and generous.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-samaritan: Stitched-thread strokes and sharp angles give Megrim a futuristic edge, every line kept to one measured thickness. Noto Sans Samaritan fills its curves with daylight, so long reading goes smoothly.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-saurashtra: Megrim looks like letters bent from a single length of wire, angular and futuristic, with a skyward x-height line. Noto Sans Saurashtra keeps counters connected outward, so long text flows.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-sc: Megrim holds every stroke, diagonals included, to a single measured thickness. It makes striking display lines, while Noto Sans SC, the sans-serif here, favors chalky curves that stop short of closing.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-sharada: Megrim is all angles and monoweight lines, a futuristic look from the first glance. But Noto Sans Sharada keeps its c forms open and its lowercase bulky, which steadies long reading.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-sinhala: Noto Sans Sinhala lays a thick, dark stripe of lowercase through every line, curve endings well apart. But Megrim handles striking, angular display lines, its diagonals carrying the stems' heft, while this plain sans does the steady reading.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-soyombo: Noto Sans Soyombo has a sizable x-height and curves with wide, unclosed mouths. Megrim, a futuristic display face of ribbon-like constant strokes, excels at sharp headings, while the plain sans carries the reading.
